group and 25% of participants (6/24) receiving endoxifen experienced
at least one Grade 1 toxicity (4/16 and 2/8 in endoxifen 10 mg and
20 mg groups, respectively). The most common toxicity was dry or

are shown in Table S2. These symptoms did not lead to discontinuation
of treatment.
Secondary endpoint- other adverse events
Participants who reported other adverse events included 2/8 (25%)
in placebo, 4/16 (25%) in endoxifen 10 mg, and 2/8 (25%) in endoxifen
20 mg arm (Table 3 and Table S3). All but two were Grade 1 events with
probable or possible attribution to study drug, consisting of common
minor symptoms (headache, night sweats, hot flashes, nausea). Grade 2
events reported in the endoxifen groups were both attributed as possibly
related: 1 vaginal yeast infection in endoxifen 10 mg arm and 1 breast
pain in endoxifen 20 mg arm. There were no serious adverse events that
led to discontinuation of treatment.

We also explored other variables that may have affected endoxifen
exposure to breast tissue. These included 1) breast size (large vs. small

calculated from the intercept-only model).
Secondary endpoint- Change in tamoxifen-responsive circulating
biomarkers
To test whether transdermal application of endoxifen (10 mg or
20 mg) induces systemic effect, we measured changes in IGF-1 and
SHBG which are established biomarkers of tamoxifen-response. No sig
nificant changes of IGF-1 and SHBG were observed by dose level
(Table S5).

3.2. Primary endpoint-local dermal toxicity at the Gel application site
Thirty-two intent-to-treat participants were evaluated for local
dermal toxicity. Drug related dermal toxicity is reported in Table 2 and
Table S2. No drug-related dermal toxicity was observed in the placebo
group and 25% of participants (6/24) receiving endoxifen experienced
at least one Grade 1 toxicity (4/16 and 2/8 in endoxifen 10 mg and
20 mg groups, respectively). The most common toxicity was dry or
itching skin and lasted for minutes to days. Details of onset and duration
are shown in Table S2. These symptoms did not lead to discontinuation
of treatment.
3.3. Secondary endpoint- other adverse events
Participants who reported other adverse events included 2/8 (25%)
in placebo, 4/16 (25%) in endoxifen 10 mg, and 2/8 (25%) in endoxifen
20 mg arm (Table 3 and Table S3). All but two were Grade 1 events with

minor symptoms (headache, night sweats, hot flashes, nausea). Grade 2
events reported in the endoxifen groups were both attributed as possibly
related: 1 vaginal yeast infection in endoxifen 10 mg arm and 1 breast
pain in endoxifen 20 mg arm. There were no serious adverse events that
led to discontinuation of treatment.
Quality of life parameters were assessed using the BESS question-
naire at study entry (baseline) and on the day prior to surgery (post-
treatment). Since three women withdrew before surgery, 29 completed
their BESS questionnaire at both time points. The changes are summa-
rized in Table 3. Overall, no change was observed in all arms, but pla-
cebo participants reported higher vasomotor scores, and bladder scores
were improved in the 20 mg endoxifen-treated participants.
3.4. Secondary endpoint-Endoxifen distribution within the breast and in
plasma
Of the 29 participants who underwent surgery, 7 did not use the
required minimum of 80% of doses by gel weight (2 Placebo, 4 endox-
ifen 10 mg, and 1 endoxifen 20 mg), resulting in 22 protocol-adherent
participants. The gel usage is summarized in Fig. S1. Breast tissue
samples (Fig. 2A) and the matching plasma sample were available from
20/22 adherent participants (5 placebo, 11 endoxifen 10 mg, and 4
endoxifen 20 mg). Tumor samples were also available from 6 partici-
pants in the 10 mg endoxifen arm for drug quantitation. Therefore, we
report the median (E/Z)-endoxifen concentration for 15 protocol-
adherent endoxifen-treated participants in Fig. 2B. Overall, trans-
dermal endoxifen absorption was low. The median per-patient concen-
tration, defined as median concentration across all sampled locations in
one or both breasts, was 0.6 ng/g (IQR 0.4–1.6). The median per-patient
concentration of five non-adherent participants was also 0.6 ng/g (IQR
0.3–0.7). When comparing tissue to plasma concentrations overall, we
found that the median per-patient breast endoxifen concentration of
0.6 ng/g (IQR 0.4–1.6) was three-fold higher (p < 0.001) than the me-
dian plasma endoxifen concentration of 0.2 ng/mL (IQR 0.2–0.2).
The median ratio of (Z)-endoxifen to (E)-endoxifen concentration in
the five benign breast tissue sampling locations was 1.50 (IQR
0.96–2.54, p < 0.05 for all locations), and was unchanged when five
tumor samples with drug concentration data were included: 1.53 (IQR
0.96–2.54). There was no clear dose-dependent accumulation of
endoxifen in breast samples when comparing concentrations between 10
and 20 mg arms. In plasma, the median concentration of (Z)-endoxifen
was significantly lower in the 10 mg group (0.2 ng/mL, IQR 0.2–0.2),
than in the 20 mg group (0.3 ng/mL, IQR 0.2–0.6) (p = 0.04). (E)-
endoxifen was not identified in the plasma of any participants.
We did not observe significant differences in the median endoxifen
concentrations between breasts for bilateral mastectomy cases (Fig. 2B).
We also explored other variables that may have affected endoxifen
exposure to breast tissue. These included 1) breast size (large vs. small &
medium), 2) the use of tumescence solution during mastectomy, 3) BMI,
4) tissue composition such as % adiposity and % epithelium of each
tissue sample collected, and 5) presence of tumor (tumor-bearing vs.
tumor-free breast). None of these factors appeared to influence endox-
ifen concentration within the breast, and concentrations in the deepest
location were in the same range as more superficial sites (Table S4 and
Fig. 2B). There was moderate correlation of breast endoxifen concen-
tration within participants (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.55,
calculated from the intercept-only model).

biomarkers
To test whether transdermal application of endoxifen (10 mg or
20 mg) induces systemic effect, we measured changes in IGF-1 and
SHBG which are established biomarkers of tamoxifen-response. No sig-
nificant changes of IGF-1 and SHBG were observed by dose level
(Table S5).
